findings: The complete four-path prepared diff was read. Node::exact_rational changes only its Int branch; One, Ratio and unsupported composite behavior are unchanged.

The new constructor is crate-private. Zero and signed one return the same canonical owners as Rational::new. Remaining signed-word values delegate only the canonical lookup to existing small_integer; its bound remains unchanged and is not duplicated at the caller.

No BigUint is rebuilt from a primitive magnitude on a cache miss. The fallback is exactly the earlier Rational::from_bigint(n.clone()) expression for every magnitude outside the bounded table, including values beyond i64. unsigned_abs handles i64::MIN without overflow.

The helper neither refines expressions nor changes certificates, retained cache payloads, term/expansion budgets, atomic ordering or expression ownership. Existing exact wide-integer and P4 cases remain required.

The first new test compares the actual Rational sign, arbitrary-width numerator and unit denominator with independent BigInt inputs for 199 values, including both signs near eleven word/wide boundaries through 4096 bits.

The second test proves reuse of the existing canonical owners for all 129 values from -64 through 64 and distinct Rational owners for six uncached boundaries. It does not enlarge the cache or change public constructors.

The sole arithmetic.rs change is cfg(test) module wiring. The 38-line module is separate from the existing long tests.rs file. All 874 preexisting test names will be required, using the earlier 875-name instrumentation run minus its single diagnostic-only counter test.

The qualification runner uses six fixed allocation processes with the original unchanged public integer driver, 1000 inputs and all twelve phases. It preserves exact witnesses and raw printed times; no duration inference or admission follows from this qualification.
